newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - April 11.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Friday:

WASHINGTON - A federal judge declared the presidential line-item veto unconstitutional, calling Congress's ceding of such vast powers "revolutionary" and warning that it turned the division of legislative and executive branch responsibilities "on its head".

BERLIN - A German court found that the highest levels of Iran's Islamic fundamentalist government gave orders to carry out the slaying of three Kurdish dissidents and their translators nearly five years ago.

UPPERVILLE, Virginia - On a football-perfect day -- cold and clear -- Washington bade farewell to Jack Kent Cooke in a service whose solemnity was lightened by memories of the Redskins owner's cerebral saltiness.

WASHINGTON - From family leave to overseas sweatshops to campaign finance, President Clinton plans to flex his executive powers to advance his priorities during a season of inactivity on Capitol Hill.

WASHINGTON - A nine-year-old student at a Southeast Washington school was sexually assaulted during school hours Monday while she and eight other fourth-graders were unsupervised in a locked room, according to her mother.
WASHINGTON - As the D.C. school board of trustees weighs the closing of 16 schools, it has ignited a firestorm of controversy from parents and several national education specialists.
